definitions.explanation: Medicine that can only be obtained with a doctor's prescription, as opposed to over-the-counter medication.

examples.japanese: {処方薬|しょほうやく}をもらいに{薬局|やっきょく}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to the pharmacy to pick up my prescription.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}は{処方薬|しょほうやく}なので、{医師|いし}の{処方箋|しょほうせん}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.english: This medicine is a prescription drug, so you need a doctor's prescription.

examples.japanese: {処方薬|しょほうやく}は{用法|ようほう}・{用量|ようりょう}を{守|まも}って{正|ただ}しく{服用|ふくよう}してください。
examples.english: Please take prescription medicine correctly, following the prescribed dosage and instructions.

notes: In Japan, prescription medicines are dispensed at {調剤薬局|ちょうざいやっきょく} (dispensing pharmacies) separate from the hospital. The doctor writes a {処方箋|しょほうせん} (prescription), which the patient takes to a pharmacy. Contrasts with {市販薬|しはんやく} (over-the-counter medicine) and {一般用医薬品|いっぱんよういやくひん} (general-use pharmaceuticals). The verb pattern is {処方薬|しょほうやく}を{処方|しょほう}する or {処方薬|しょほうやく}を{出|だ}す (to prescribe medication).
